root_cause.text: The original commit introduced a deadlock by acquiring the card->controls_rwsem read lock inside fsl_xcvr_mode_put(), which is already called while holding the write lock on the same rwsem from the ALSA core function snd_ctl_elem_write().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and CVE description explain that "this function is called from the upper ALSA core function snd_ctl_elem_write(), which already holds the write lock on controls_rwsem for the whole put operation. So there is no need to simply hold the lock for fsl_xcvr_activate_ctl() again. Acquiring the read lock while holding the write lock in the same thread results in a deadlock and a hung task." The patch diff removes the down_read(&card->snd_card->controls_rwsem) and up_read() calls.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary read lock acquisition that could cause deadlock when activating controls.
intent_record.what: Removed down_read and up_read calls around two fsl_xcvr_activate_ctl function calls in the fsl_xcvr_mode_put function.
intent_record.how: The code no longer acquires or releases the controls_rwsem read lock when activating controls, preventing a potential deadlock if fsl_xcvr_activate_ctl internally attempts to take the write lock.

grouping_result.intent: Remove unnecessary read lock acquisition that could cause deadlock when activating controls.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly removes the read lock acquisition inside fsl_xcvr_mode_put() that causes a deadlock because it is called while the write lock is held.

candidates.rationale: Acquiring the read lock on card->snd_card->controls_rwsem while already holding the write lock (from snd_ctl_elem_write) causes a deadlock because rwsem does not support recursive locking.
Releasing the read lock is necessary to match the acquisition, but the entire locking operation is unnecessary and causes the deadlock described in the root cause.
